# Same-module steady function-attribution host

This source checkpoint implements the accepted four-file profile proposal. Actual profiling remains unreleased. No WASM instance, fixture, profile, timing, build or optimization edit ran here; only pure binary/profile fixtures, mocked process guards and read-only source/module admission are permitted. Production DSP stays frozen, candidate unselected and the 192 kHz steady RED open.

The host prepares a fresh diagnostic ID referencing the existing WASM pair. Its outer diagnostic binding indexes all 45 sources: the unchanged 37-source screen-child binding, four proposal files and these four host/parser/contract/readme files. The original child binding and its source inventory retain their exact meaning and bytes. No module is copied or rebuilt. Every new source is frozen separately. Actual original-unit, semantic, recorder, verification and first-timing proof is re-read, including historical failures.

A future separately released run has exactly two steady verification children, baseline then candidate. The screen child, Go work, closed filesystem and post-exit helpers remain unchanged. The actual Node argv explicitly adds CPU profiling with a requested 100-microsecond interval and a fresh private profile path; diagnostic umask is 077. The parent reuses the fully owned setup/selector/kill/reap/EOF guard with original 25-second Go/28-second parent/256 KiB log limits. The result validator must equal the frozen validator with only its expected argv expression replaced; it never rewrites or substitutes receipts. Entire raw verification output must match sealed source-v1 bytes, alongside every unchanged counter/PCM/state/I/O check.

The parser uses pre-stat regular-file, size and no-symlink checks before module reads, then verifies identity again on the opened file. Module input stays at most 16 MiB. It resolves actual names/function indices/code-body hashes, validates closed profile schemas and one rooted acyclic call tree, and enforces aggregate 4 MiB profile/16,384-node/65,536-sample/1,048,576-stack-step admission. An 8 MiB attribution-report limit also fails closed. Profile size is admitted after process exit; this is no preemptive write or internal V8/RSS ceiling. Oversized, missing or partial files stay RED without retries.

Reports preserve raw call frames, module function indices and body hashes, requested and observed sampling intervals, graph-root coverage, unresolved frames, self leaves, deduplicated inclusive function/edge memberships, recursion and top caller paths. Inclusive counts overlap. Actual function attribution gives no source-line or instruction-cost proof. Sampling argv and overhead differ from the timing method, so these diagnostics cannot establish comparable timing, speedup, worst callbacks, browser/physical deadlines, headroom or physical steady state. Sparse evidence cannot trigger automatic longer work, cap changes or a new optimization.

Future commands require separate Chair release: `run-profile.py prepare NEW_ID`, then `run-profile.py run ID diagnostic-approved`. Source preparation itself launches no WASM child; no run route is exercised by this checkpoint.

Source validation: 21 controls passed in 1.867 seconds, including pure binary/profile fixtures, direct diagnostic-argv/receipt negatives and five inherited mocked lifecycle/I/O controls. Python syntax and read-only 45-source/module/prerequisite admission passed. These controls exercised neither `prepare` nor `run` and launched no WASM/profile child. Future released children require the authorized execution context that permits owned process-group cleanup.
